# standards 0.0.3: highlights

The hand-written part of the release notes; scripts/release.py adds the rest.

* **A push no longer destroys an edit**: `standards-sync --push` overwrites a file only if it is missing, identical, or a version this repository committed. A file edited in place is kept and named, and `~/Code` can now link straight to this repository.
* **The standards agree with each other again**: they caught up with the workspace, and `REPO-STANDARD.md` now reads the release title from `gh`'s `name` field, which exists, instead of `title`, which does not.
* **This repository meets its own rules**: one `make check` gate runs lint, the complexity ceilings, tests at 99 percent coverage, fuzzing, a strict manual build, API and advisory checks, and a reproducible build, on Linux and macOS, Python 3.9 to 3.15.
* **Releases you can verify**: signed tags checked against `KEYS.asc`, assets with SHA-256 sums, an SBOM and SLSA provenance, and a manual at <https://sebastienrousseau.github.io/standards/>.
